Mortrack ML API v1.0.0.2

As a result of a formal scientific investigation into what is a software library; an API and; a software framework, it was determined that calling this software an API was incorrect. Therefore, all erroneous uses of the word API were changed to Library, as it better matched what this software actually is. In addition, the text of the README.md file was reworded and its code examples were corrected as it was detected that there were some misused tab spaces that produced errors when executing those codes.

Regarding my thesis project, I started and finished validating all the activation functions of the single neuron in Deep Neural Network algorithm from the CenyML library (except the raise to the 1st power activation function which I have already validated). While doing that, I determined that a neuron cannot solve for when you use a square root activation function. One hypothesis I have regarding this issue is that the square root has an infinite number of critical points and therefore, the neuron never learns with that activation function. I am basing this thought on the fact that I could not solve finding the critical point of a square root by hand and could only do it by converting its derivative to an approximation function. The approximation function I used to solve it was the Taylor series and it was because of this that I concluded that the square root function has an infinite number of critical points. This makes sense because the only way to obtain a perfect approximation with the Taylor series is if repeating the series expansion to infinite. On the other hand, I started and finished validating a classification problem when using the single neuron in Deep Neural Network algorithm from the CenyML library to make sure it will work with either its regression or classification solver. However, while doing that, I corrected the single neuron in DNN algorithm from the CenyML library with respect to not making the neuron convert the output values to binary values for its training process (it is required) and to also revert them to their original output values at the end of such process (when selecting the classification solver). Finally, I started and finished updating the content of the README.md file from the validation folder of the single neuron in DNN algorithm with respect to all the changes applied in this commit.

I corrected the one of the URLs I placed in the commented documentation of the Cplusplus Dlib implementation I made for the linear support vector machine classifier, in the validation folders. Then, I noticed that when you plug in specific hyperparameter values to the SVM functions of the Dlib and Python libraries, they solve the model iteratively to find the best solution through exploring several hyperparameter values. Therefore, I made sure that all of them did not had one specified so that this iteration was made because that would be fair compared to my algorithm since it does not require such iteration at all, except for the gaussian Kernel, which is the only for that I allowed to have specific values of hyperparameters so that it can be fair to compare them. However, I think I will discard the scikit-learn results with the rbf Kernel because I noticed that the hyperparameter used there (which is gamma) cannot be manually assigned by the implementer. As a result, it would be unfair to evaluate such method with mine because if I were to attempt an iteration with my gaussian method to be able to compare it, then that would also lead to bias. This is because I can attempt to intentionally fit the best possible iteration so that the results favor me, which is why I will most certainly discard the gaussian Kernel results obtained with scikit-learn. Moreover, I started and finished developing the Dlib rbf Kernel SVM algorithm in its Cplusplus version but could not apply other types of Kernels because I was getting errors saying that those Kernels were not know. I made sure to follow what the documentation said, as for what I was able to understand, but it seems I was either not able to apply them or they simply are not available in the SVM made by Dlib. Finally, I started and finished writing the content of the README.md file that explains the purpose of the files contained in the validation folder KernelMachineClassificaiton and how to use them.
